articleTitle: Parameter Control System for a Nuclear Power Plant Based on Fiber-Optic Sensors and Communication Lines
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: A control system for values of various physical parameters has been developed for a nuclear power plant with VVER-1000 reactor. Various designs of fiber-optic sensors are considered, which are integrated into a single monitoring and control system without additional devices. The measurement results are presented. The necessity of continuing research and development in this direction is substantiated.

articleTitle: Survey on Beamforming Techniques and Integrated Circuits for 5G Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Electronic scanning is widely used in radar systems. Fifth generation (5G) communication systems are highly relying on the same principle. Different beamforming techniques, such as digital, analog and hybrid, are studied and compared in theory by many authors during the search of optimal architecture in sense of energy and spectral efficiency. Several integrated solutions have been designed and published by university researches and commercial companies. In this paper some of the recent publications about beamforming techniques and integrated circuits for sub-6 GHz and sub-30 GHz are discussed and compared.

articleTitle: Positioning for Location-Aware Beamforming in 5G Ultra-Dense Networks
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: 5G ultra-dense radio networks enhance utilization of spatial dimension by wide implementation of location-aware beamforming and interference mitigation techniques. Successful realization of simultaneous transmission and reception is possible by means of preliminary positioning of neighboring user equipment. Contribution of the current research is positioning accuracy limits estimation of user equipment using direction of arrival measurement processing in three-dimensional space with metrics of Cramer-Rao lower bound ellipsoid. Resulting accuracy limits were analyzed and visualized to assist in proper access nodes layout.

articleTitle: Charge-coupled Device with Integrated Electron Multiplication for Low Light Level Imaging
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Design of the charge-coupled device with the effect of electron multiplication is proposed. The increase of signal-to-noise ratio under low illumination as compared to the device without electron multiplication effect is demonstrated. The measurements at various temperature conditions and supply voltages have been carried out. The optimal operating mode of the proposed device is suggested.

articleTitle: New Pulse Shapes for Partial Response Signaling to Outperform Faster-than-Nyquist Signaling
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Faster-than-Nyquist (FTN) signaling is the promising idea that theoretically provides a significant increase in the spectral efficiency without energy loss. The gain is achieved through incorporating intersymbol interference (ISI) by simply increasing symbol rate. Another way to increase spectral efficiency is to use pulses assuming incorporating ISI. It is commonly called Partial Response (PR) signaling. Both approaches face certain difficulties in the signal processing as the conventional processing chain including a matched filter causes colored noise. Also, FTN signaling and PR signaling achieve declared gains only asymptotically, i.e. at very low values of the bit error rate (BER) and a high computational complexity of the detection algorithms. In this paper, we propose two methods of signal processing with ISI. Both of them cause white noise. The former is suitable for simulation and the latter is suitable for practical implementation. Additionally, we propose a new optimization criterion for synthesizing pulses for PR signaling. It is shown in the article that PR signaling with the pulses proposed by us outperform FTN signaling and PR signaling with other known optimal pulses. Moreover, it is achieve the Mazo limit at BER = 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−4</sup> and with low computational complexity of signal detection.

articleTitle: Radiomics: Extracting more Features using Endoscopic Imaging
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Cancer is the leading cause of death in the world and delayed detection being the cause of the most significant factor for its high mortality rate. Computers can help radiologists in analyzing medical images and detection of cancer. Radiomics refers to the computerized extraction of information from medical images and provides the potential for making cancer screening with high rapid and more accurate using machine learning algorithms. Endoscopic imaging and X-ray imaging (Computed tomography) are two common methods used in medical imaging. In this paper, the advantages and limitations of endoscopic and CT scan images discussed. Then the features that can be extracted from endoscopic and CT scans are discussed and finally these two imaging methods are considered and compared to use for computer-aided detection systems.

articleTitle: Implementation of Synthetic Aperture Radar Processing Algorithms on the Jetson TX1 Platform
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The paper describes the implementation and testing of two synthetic aperture radar processing algorithms on Jetson TX1 platform using the ArrayFire parallel library. Their execution time was compared when using Jetson’s multicore CPU and GPU. Comparison was also done with a desktop computer. It was discovered that GPU computing on Jetson is faster for both algorithms compared to its CPU. However, the results for a desktop computer depend on the type of an algorithm.

articleTitle: Criteria for Selection Envelope Tracking Power Supply Parameters for High Peak-to-Average Power Ratio Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The signals used in telecommunication systems have a high peak-to-average power ratio. To increase the efficiency of power amplifiers of such signals, an envelope tracking method can be applied. In this case, an envelope tracking power supply (ETPS) can be implemented on the basis of a multi-cell switched-mode power amplifier. This allows not only to partially compensate non-linear distortions associated with the use of the switch mode, but also to expand the ETPS bandwidth by increasing the number of cells. It is noted that in the case when output power of a single cell is limited, the possibility of increasing the output power can be regarded as an important advantage of a multi-cell power amplifier. It is emphasized that the increase in number of cells leads to the raise of the mass and dimensions of ETPS. The main factors that limit the multi-cell ETPS bandwidth are noted in the paper. These include errors in synchronization of cells control signals and dispersion in the implementation of the LPF inductances. The influence of these factors leads to significant increase in side spectra at frequencies that are multiples of the sampling frequency. Recommendations on choosing the rational number of cells, that will allow us to show up all the multi-cell ETPS’s advantages, are given.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Finite Discrete RRC-Pulse Parameters to Simulate DVB-S2 with LDM
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: This paper analyzes the impact of Root Raised Cosine (RRC) filter design for Non Orthogonal Multiplexing (NOM) satellite applications. Specifically, this study has been carried out for a special case of NOM in broadcast environments, combining the technique Layered Division Multiplexing (LDM) with the DVB-S2X standard. The paper first defines the RRC discrete representation parameters and uses simulations to optimize their values. The goal is to minimize Inter-Symbol Interference (ISI) and make the spectrum shape compliant with DVB-S2X spectral mask requirements. Simulations also show that it is possible to define parameters values of discrete RRC pulse to obtain Peak to Average Power Ratio (PAPR) closer than 0.01 dB to the theoretical result for continuous pulse.

articleTitle: FPGA Design and Implementation of DVB-S2/S2X LDPC Encoder
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: A new FPGA architecture of the DVB-S2/S2X LDPC FEC encoder with low number of resources consumption is proposed. The encoder is full rate compatible and supports all code rates from DVB-S2/S2X standards. In addition, all frame types (normal, medium and short) are supported. The proposed architecture is based on iterative addresses calculation of parity bits accumulators and actively reuses parity calculators and parity storage. The Kintex FPGA implementation of the proposed architecture is done resulting in less than 3000 look-up-tables and flip-flops and only 6 block memories usage.

articleTitle: Determination of Noise Components in Laser Correlation Spectroscopic Devices for Signal-to-Noise Ratio Estimation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Laser correlation spectroscopy is a powerful method of estimating the size of nanoparticles. It was shown that uncertainty of size determination is strongly influenced by signal-to-noise ratio, achieved in the designed scheme. In this work, we consider signal-to-noise ratio for one realization of laser correlation spectrometer and review noise parameters of main elements of laser correlation spectrometer. Presented principles could be used for signal-to-noise ratio calculation for other types of dynamic light scattering devices.

articleTitle: Determination of Electrophoretic Mobilities by DLS: Homodyne vs Heterodyne Setup
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: In the work, determination of electrophoretic mobilities of microspheres by means of dynamic light scattering has been performed. We compared two types of experimental setup for dynamic light scattering under electric field: homodyne and heterodyne. The homodyne setup was implemented with a TIR prism, the heterodyne setup was realized conventionally using a beam splitter. Sample spectrograms of intensity variations in heterodyne and homodyne setups have been obtained. Electrophoretic mobility has been calculated using spectral analysis based on the Doppler shift frequency. If the differences in the effective angles for Doppler effects are accounted for, both approaches produce comparable estimates of electrophoretic mobilities.

articleTitle: The Influence of the Magnetic Field Direction Variations on the Frequency Stability of a Gas Cell Atomic Clock
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: This article presents the results of direct experimental measurements of the static shielding coefficients of the magnetic shield of the small commercial rubidium frequency standard (SCRFS), and also predicts the possible effect of magnetic field variations on the accuracy of the atomic clock in the onboard equipment of communication satellites. The experiments were carried out under the conditions of frequency control of the SCRFS, placed in a system of three orthogonally oriented Helmholtz coils designed to compensate for the geomagnetic field and to create a variable magnetic field of ultra-low frequency. Frequency SCRFS (volume 75×75×35 mm) was measured by the frequency counter CNT-85R with built-in rubidium frequency standard with a relative ten-second stability on the level of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-12</sup>. The relative stability of a ten-second SCRFS was ~3•10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-12</sup>. Measurements of the shielding static coefficient of the SCRFS were carried out under the conditions of the vertical component compensation of the geomagnetic laboratory field (~16 µT) with the constant magnetic field inclusion (~188 µT) created by Helmholtz coils along the axis (~10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) and across the axis (~10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>) the SCRFS. The calculated value of the working magnetic field inside the screen was equal to 3 µT. Research results allow to make an unambiguous conclusion about the probable effect of geomagnetic field variations on the atomic clocks accuracy of the communication satellites onboard equipment, which requires an appropriate correction of the processed information.

articleTitle: Output Voltage PWM Conversion Inaccuracies in Envelope Tracking Power Supply for High Peak-to-Average Power Ratio Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: When amplifying signals with a high peak-to- average power ratio, the envelope tracking method is widely used to increase the efficiency of power amplifiers. When designing a control device for an envelope tracking power supply (ETPS), it is relevant to form control signals using digital methods. The paper considers errors of envelope signal forming with multi-cell ETPS, which are caused by a number of factors. These include: digital representation of control pulses PWM-sequences parameters, inaccuracies of cell synchronization, dispersion of parameters of transistors and elements of low-pass filter (LPF). It is shown that bits number chosen to represent PWM pulses in digital form contributes to the appearance of parasitic components in the output spectrum of the ETPS, which get into the LPF bandwidth. The dispersion of the transistors time parameters, inaccuracies of the PWM forming synchronization and dispersion of LPF inductances lead to a significant increase of the side spectral components that are multiples of the PWM frequency. Satisfying the conditions formulated in the paper, which are associated with increasing the accuracy of control signals forming and decreasing the dispersion of the LPF inductances, will make full use of the multi-cell ETPS advantages.

articleTitle: Computational Complexity Analysis of SEFDM Time and Frequency Domain Equalizers
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The paper addresses a comparison of computational complexity of time domain and frequency domain equalizers for non-orthogonal multicarrier (SEFDM, Spectrally Efficient Frequency Division Multiplexing) signals. The comparison is done for various values of subcarrier frequency spacing parameter and number of subcarriers.

articleTitle: Trends and Challenges in Broadcast and Broadband Convergence
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The convergence between broadcast and broadband networks has drawn significant attention since the very beginning of their coexistence. Nonetheless, a real cooperation framework has not been successfully implemented yet due to the limits of the contemporary technologies. However, the newly proposed architectures for both broadband and broadcast allow the development of new solutions for multimedia and entertainment content delivery in multi-tier radio access networks. In fact, the convergence of broadcast and broadband technologies is one of the solutions that has been already proposed. Convergence would offer a better spectrum efficiency, improving the quality of service of the broadcasted services to mobile receivers. The main contribution of this paper is a comprehensive state of the arte of the past efforts and on top of that, the definition of the most relevant use cases for several future scenarios.

articleTitle: The Analytical Model for Calculating Distortions in the Envelope Tracking Power Supply
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Amplification of signals with a high peak-to-average power ratio is accompanied by decreasing of the radio transmitter's efficiency, which can be increased with the help of the envelope tracking method. A multi-cell switched-mode power amplifier can be used as an envelope tracking power supply, which, on the one hand, allows us to expand the bandwidth and decrease requirements for output filter, on the other hand, it is characterized by non-linear distortions, due to the features of the switched-mode operating. Their levels can be estimated using simulation. However, the simulation time spent can be tens of minutes or even several hours, especially when trying to take into account the statistical dispersion of some parameters of the envelope tracking power supply. This is due to using complex non-linear models of the transistors, the number of which in the envelope tracking power supply can reach several dozens. Time spent can be reduced by using an approximate analytical model. However, its disadvantage is the low accuracy associated with assumptions about the non-inertial transistors and, as a rule, about the lack of the simulated device’s parameters dispersion. The paper presents an analytical model of a multi-cell envelope tracking power supply, which takes into account the digital conversion of its input voltage and reference voltage, the inertial properties of real transistor, the on-state transistor voltage and the dispersion of the output filter inductances. In addition, this model implements a statistical analysis of the transistors parameters dispersion. This allows us to provide a difference with the results of an experiment less than 10% with a time spent as much as 3…6 times less than using simulation. Such accuracy, combined with low time spent, allows using the represented analytical model in engineering calculations of the envelope tracking power supply.

articleTitle: Comparison of the Spectral and Energy Efficiency of FTN Signals Based on RRC Pulses and Obtained by the Optimization Method
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The paper is devoted to the study of signals obtained as a solution of the optimization task. This approach can be used in Faster-Than-Nyquist (FTN) signaling to provide extremely high transmission rates. However, an increase in transmission rate results in the strong intersymbol interference (ISI), affecting energy efficiency, especially for commonly used square-root-raised-cosine pulses. The main advantage of optimal signal is in controlled ISI level for different rates and pulse durations. We consider application of Viterbi Algorithm for optimal FTN signals reception. Using the Viterbi algorithm for receiving signals with increased duration and intersymbol interference provides close to potential BER performance, while symbol rate is higher the Nyquist limit. The paper provides the comparison of spectral and time characteristics for the optimal and root-raised-cosine pulses for different cases (pulse durations, roll-off factors).

articleTitle: A Comparison of 6-bit Non-universal Switching Schemes for Unary DACs
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: This paper is devoted to a systematic error compensation in unary digital-to-analog converters. The compensation is achieved by a special switching order of weighting elements – a switching scheme. An overview of several recently published 6-bit non-universal switching schemes is presented. A simulation of integral nonlinearity is done to estimate efficiency of each switching scheme. A comparison shows that switching scheme "Xueqing Li" is the most effective in all test conditions.

articleTitle: Simulation of Flexible Thermoelectric Generators Based on Bi2Te3/Sb2Te3 Synthesized by Electrochemical Deposition Method
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Thermoelectric generator simulations and comparative analysis of output parameters have been carried out for two geometries (Y-structure and П-structure with a flexible base) at different temperatures. Electrochemically deposited films of bismuth telluride Bi2Te3 and antimony telluride Sb2Te3 were used as functional materials. The following results have been achieved: the maximal output power of a Y-structure generator at the temperature range from 10 to 100 <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup>C made up P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf> = 324 μW, and the output power of П-structure generator made up P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf> = 118 μW. The specific maximal output power of a Y-structure generator made up P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf>/S = 12.47 μW/mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, the specific maximal output power of a П-structure made up P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf>/S = 4.54 μW/mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The thermoelectric generator based on Y-structure has proved to possess the specific output power exceeding 2.7 times the one of the conventional structural thermal generator.

articleTitle: Walking Robot with Propulsors Based on IPMC Actuators
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The goal of this work was to investigate the possibility of using an ionic polymer-metal composite actuator (IPMC-actuator) as the main element of a motion drive for a walking robotic system. An actuator module was developed, which consists of two actuators connected in parallel and allowing a "leg" of the robotic system to move in two planes. Due to the use of an IMPC-actuator it was possible to develop a robotic system with dimensions of 118x114x62.4 mm, moving at a speed of 1 mm/s with a step of 33 mm and a mass of 70 g.

articleTitle: The Method for Protection of Sensitive Fiber Optic Components from Environmental Noise and Vibration Impacts
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Fiber optic components, such as fiber optic interferometers, fiber sensors and fiber lasers have high level of sensitivity to environmental acoustic and vibration noise due to elasto-optical effect and fiber elongation under pressure. For most applications this effect is undesirable and it should be reduced for proper operation of fiber optic system. The proposed method for reducing the fiber components environmental noise sensitivity level is based on the implementation of two-layer protective construction. The experimental test confirmed its effectiveness of undesirable impact suppression at the level from -3.2 to -19 dB relatively to the acoustic sensitivity level of bare optical fiber sample. The effectiveness appeared to be directly proportional to the acoustic pressure level. This fact allows us to implement proposed construction as an acoustic shock absorber or an acoustic filter with external impact level dependent transfert characteristic for sensitive fiber optic components.

articleTitle: The Effectiveness of Tone Reservation Method for Peak-to-Average Power Ratio Reduction of SEFDM Signals with Optimal Envelopes
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The modification of Tone Reservation method has been used to reduce peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) of multicarrier signals with non-orthogonal frequency spacing (Spectrally Efficient Frequency Division Multiplexing, SEFDM). Multi-frequency signals are used in combination with a smoothed envelope in order to reduce the level of out-of-band emissions (OOBE). Simulation results show that, when additional subcarriers occupy 10% of bandwidth, PAPR reduction in average is equal to 1.25 dB, but spectral efficiency also decreases 1.1 times for the OFDM signals. In the case of SEFDM, with the advantage of having greater spectral efficiency, SEFDM signal can compensate for this drawback.

articleTitle: Manufacturing Method and Stability Research of the Fiber Quarter-Wave Plate for Fiber Optic Current Sensor
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: One of the most important elements of the optical scheme of the fiber-optic current sensor is a quarter-wave plate, which converts two orthogonal linearly polarized modes into circularly polarized modes, which propagate further in the sensitive element of the sensor. To maintain the integrity of the system and ensure high-precision measurements, it is important that the plate is made of fiber, and its length is equal to a quarter of the beat length with an accuracy of a hundredth of a millimeter, which is technically very difficult to achieve. This article discusses a model of an electronically adjusted quarter-wave plate, which made it possible to check the operability of the fiber-optic current sensor circuit. The article also describes a method for manufacturing of quarter-wave plate, presents the results of temperature tests of plates of different lengths in the current sensor circuit, and estimates the effect of the quarter-wave plate temperature on the measurement error.

articleTitle: The Method of Reducing of the Measurement Error of the Amplitude Spectrum Based on the Sliding DFT Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Currently, the methods which are based on the application of the window functions and sampling rate converters (SRC) are used to reduce the effect of "spectrum leakage" for real electric networks. Both approaches involve a number of practical difficulties. In the case of application of the window functions, the complexity of the spectrum measurement algorithm increases. In this case a decrease in the measurement error of the spectral components is achieved by increasing the measurement error of the fundamental spectral component. When using SRC an additional operations are required to measure the frequency of the signal and to make digital interpolation. In this case, the task of analyzing the resulting measurement error is substantially complicated. In the present work, an analysis of the measurement error of the amplitude spectrum by using a sliding discrete Fourier transform is performed. A method is proposed that allows to reduce the measurement error of the amplitude spectrum by applying output filtration of the measurement results of the amplitude spectrum. The obtained analytical relations allows to estimate the measurement error of the amplitude spectrum. Requirements have been developed for an additional filter that provides filtration of the measurement signal of the amplitude spectrum. By using the Simulink software package, a simulation model of the proposed measurement method is performed. The reliability of the obtained expressions is confirmed by comparing the results which are obtained by the analytical relationships and by the simulation model.

articleTitle: Compensation of Fiber Quarter-Wave Plate Temperature Deviation in Fiber Optic Current Sensor
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The paper describes the problem of fiber quarter-wave plate temperature dependency, its influence on the fiber optic current sensors (FOCS) output error, the method of this error compensation, and the results of this method implementation.

articleTitle: Utilization of FBG Interrogator for the Analysis of Multimode Fiber Interferometer Signals Induced by Laser Frequency Modulation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Multimode fiber interferometer signals caused by laser optical frequency scanning have been investigated for different lengths of parabolic- and step-index multimode fibers with different excitation conditions. Fiber Bragg grating interrogator based on tunable light source was utilized in the experiments. Experimental results match qualitatively with theoretical dependences: parabolic-index core profile leads to significant decrease of interferometer sensitivity to laser frequency changes in comparison with step-index profile, while the sensitivity increases with the increase of multimode fiber length and with the number of excited modes. The use of widely-tuned scanning laser of the FBG interrogator enables to exclude the necessity of using long fibers that simplifies the experiments.

articleTitle: Study of Bubble Errors Conversion in a Modified ROM Encoder
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Special algorithm for the correctness validation of the conversion in Modified ROM Encoder was proposed and implemented. A comparison of bubble tolerance for basic ROM and modified ROM encoders was also carried out.

articleTitle: Fiber-Optic Fabry-Perot Interferometric Sensor for Pulse Wave Registration
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The paper presents a fiber-optic pulse wave sensor based on extrinsic Fabry-Perot interferometer. The interferometer is formed by the end faces of optical fibers, glued to a glass capillary. The sensor was interrogated by means of spectral interferometry approach. The features of the pulse wave signal as small as 100 pm were clearly observed in the demodulated waveform. The proposed sensor can be used for medical diagnostics and vital signs monitoring.

articleTitle: Efficiency of a Class DE Power Amplifier for RF Signals with High Peak-to-Average Power Ratio
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The class DE power amplifier (PA) has high efficiency only with certain parameters of the input signal, frequency and load resistance. Therefore, amplification of signals with high peak-to-average power ratio causes a violation of the zero voltage switching (ZVS) condition. This can reduce the efficiency of class DE PA. In particular, by using the analytical model it was found that PA efficiency depends significantly upon the value of transistor grading coefficient of a body junction diode. Moreover, after simulation, the range of the voltage was determined, at which the ZVS condition must be satisfied in order to minimize the power loss.

articleTitle: Phase Difference Measurement of the Target Signals of Sensing Elements in the Push-Pull Fiber Optic Interferometric Acoustic and Vibration Sensors
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: In this paper we consider a fiber-optic interferometric push-pull sensor containing 4 spirals of a single-mode optical fiber. Experimental determination of the phase difference of the target acoustic and vibrational signals is performed independently for each of the spirals. The sensor was placed into acoustic chamber, each of the sensor sensitive elements was connected to the interrogation system in an optical time domain multiplexing (TDM) scheme, and the phase difference of the target signals between 4 sensitive elements was determined. Additionally, similar measurements were performed when connecting the sensor to a vibrating test bench. The experimental results turned out to be close to theoretical values; under the influence of the target acoustic signal, the external and internal plates had counter-phase signals.

articleTitle: Algorithm for Studying Thermal Transients
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The article considers the problem of reducing the influence of thermal transients on the experimental results. An algorithm is proposed and a scheme is developed for temperature measurements of thermal transients with high accuracy using Pt1000 series thermistors. For the algorithm used, a technique and a processing scheme for the measurement results based on the microcontroller are developed. Research results are presented.

articleTitle: An Approach of Identifying Polymers With Fluorescence Lifetime Imaging
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Nowadays, fluorescence lifetime measurements and the method of fluorescence lifetime imaging are already state of the art in biomedical research. Also first investigations show that polymers could be identified due to their endogenous fluorescent lifetime. Thus an approach of identifying polymers with fluorescence lifetime imaging is done in this contribution. Therefore, four different polymers are examined and evaluated with statistical methods in order to determine their specific fluorescence lifetimes.

articleTitle: Laser ranging of the Atmospheric Aerosol and Determination of its Disperse Composition
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: It has been fulfilled the assessment of the differential easing method for the remote measurement of the aerosol pollution disperse composition parameters in the atmospheric boundary layer over the industrial enterprise. Laser attenuation signals at three wavelengths have been measured using the developed aerosol lidar system, from which average values of the volume and surface diameter of aerosol particles of cement have been obtained. The diameter average value of 0.61±0.04 μm and relative accuracy ε=11% have been calculated.

Author Keywords: particles average volume and superficial diameter

articleTitle: Laser Frequency Noise Measurement by Forming an Interference Signal with Subcarrier Frequency
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The paper presents a method for measuring laser frequency noise spectrum with the use of unbalanced fiber-optic interferometer and auxiliary phase modulation, forming a subcarrier signal at the interferometer output. The main features of the proposed method are analyzed. The paper also presents the results of experimental validation of the proposed method by measuring laser frequency noise of a high-coherent optical fiber laser.

articleTitle: Health Analysis and Diagnostic Program Synthesis for Avionics Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: This paper deals with the approach that can be applied for the Integrated System Health Management (ISHM) implementation in avionics, i.e. a health analysis using a data presentation in the form of aggregated models, and equipment diagnostics methods which involve a synthesis of the optimal and suboptimal diagnostics programs by the dynamic programming and branch and bound methods.

articleTitle: Secured Environment for Cloud Integrated Fog and Mist Architecture
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: One of the most overgrown research domains is Fog computing in which cloud services are strikingly extended to the network's edge, simultaneously inducing likelihood of computations, communications, as well as storage services in nearness to the end use in order to get adapted to the issues of low transfer speed, high latency and network congestion towards maximum network throughput specifically with the rapid growth in demands in the Internet of Things (IoT). The primary concern of research community is dedicated to development of security lightweight cryptography approaches in the middleware of mobile cloud. This exploration study aims to explore enormous points of view of Fog computing based IoT applications execution and processing security and trustworthiness from perspective of performance testing based models. The study also improves the design issues of security and testing in correspondence to IoT through efficient utilization of IoT paradigms. The proposed solution has been compared to measurable modules and noted that using iFogSim has the most secure environment to perform the topologies for Fog and Mist computing.

articleTitle: Synthesis and Study of Zinc Oxide Layers Sensitized by Colloidal Nanocrystals
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: In this paper, we present a technique for the synthesis of gas sensitive layers based on zinc oxide nanowires sensitized by colloidal AgInS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/ZnS nanocrystals. Zinc oxide nanowires were synthesized by hydrothermal method. Layers of ZnO nanowires were placed in an aqueous solution of nanocrystals for 4 hours. Study of gas-sensitive properties of sensitized layers showed a significant increase in their response to isopropanol vapors at room temperature compared to zinc oxide nanowires.

articleTitle: Degradation of NiO-GNPs Electrochromic Coating
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The work represents some aspects of plasmonic electrochromism at NiO-GNPs structure. It was demonstrated that NiO-GNPs nanocomposite made by formation of gold islands and MOCVD process have 35% more bleached state than NiO coatings synthesized at the same conditions. Also, it was found that after about 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> cycles the type of coating coloration changed from anodically colorated state to cathodically colorated one.

articleTitle: Residual Stresses in Optical Fiber Preforms with Strengthening Titanium-Silicate Glass Layers
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The paper presents the results of the residual stresses reconstruction and their influence on the refractive index profile (RIP) in a number of strengthened preforms for single-mode optical fibers. Strengthening layers were formed by external and internal vapor-phase deposition of titaniumsilicate glass. It was found that an increase in the concentration of TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> in the strengthening layer leads to significant piezooptical distortions of the RIP due to large tensile stresses in the core.

articleTitle: Optical Methods for Periodontitis Early Rapid Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The results of experimental study of periodontitis early diagnosis using optical methods (Raman spectroscopy and confocal microscopy) are presented. The features of Raman spectra of saliva for the studied groups of patients have been established. It is shown that the main markers of periodontitis are the lines of 1556 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> and 1738 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>. The results of the research using Raman spectroscopy have been compared with the microscopic analysis.

articleTitle: Development of Edge Computing Distribution Method in VANET Based Real-Time Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: This paper describes VANET network architecture based on SDN/MEC systems to reduce network load and traffic density . In this work, we examined the possibility of temporarily placing the application to the RSU for reducing the load on the network backhaul. The condition for temporary placement of the application is based on data on congestion of road sections from Google Map & Yandex monitoring systems and current Internet traffic statistics. The proposed architecture allows optimal use of the RSU/MEC resources and significantly reduces the load on the backhaul and Latency.

articleTitle: Temperature Evolution of Atomic Dynamics in Chemically Ordered Lead Scandium Niobate Studied by Inelastic Neutron Scattering
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Preliminary results of inelastic neutron scattering in chemically ordered Pb(Sc<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</inf>Nb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>/<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>)O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> (PSN) are reported. It is shown that neutron spectra, obtained around 220 node in $\left[ {1\bar 10} \right]$ direction, are characterised by intense central peak and broad phonon resonances at all studied temperatures. It has been found that TO in-plane polarised phonons do not demonstrate any softening. On the contrary, clear growth of TO phonon energy was detected for all temperatures. Intensity of the central peak continuously grows on cooling. Observed critical dynamics scenario completely differs from the expected one for relaxor or ferroelectric material. We believe our observations could bring new insights in the understanding of the microscopic origin of the relaxor phenomena.

articleTitle: A Study of Dual-Directional SCR with Low Dynamic Resistance and High Holding Voltage for Low-Voltage Application
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: A silicon controlled rectifier (SCR)-based dual- directional electrostatic discharge (ESD) protection device with low on-resistance high holding voltage and low on-resistance for low-voltage applications is proposed. It can also be applied to high-speed-interface applications, such as the Internet of things, wearable devices, and mobile processors. The proposed dual- directional ESD protection device has a great current-driving capacity because of its underneath on-resistance and highly effective second breakdown current in comparison with the original SCR-based dual-directional ESD protection device. Therefore, the proposed dual-directional ESD protection device can provide a low impedance discharge path in the NS, ND, PS, and PD ESD stress modes.

articleTitle: Adaptive TDOA Estimation for Positioning in NB-IoT
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Narrowband-Internet of Things (NB-IoT) is the low power wide area (LPWA) technology developed by 3GPP for low-cost and power-efficient IoT devices. Due to the IoT requirements for efficiency, this scheme operates with limited specifications (bandwidth, sampling rate, etc.) that can limit the positioning performance based on observed time difference of arrival (OTDOA). In order to improve OTDOA-based localization performance in multipath scenarios, this paper presents an adaptive-threshold-based TDOA estimator with a previous successive interference cancellation (SIC) stage for NBIoT systems. Simulation results show that the proposed solution outperforms the classical OTDOA scheme in different multipath channels.

articleTitle: Phase Noise Simulation of Microwave Reference Oscillator Based on the MMIC Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: In this article the computer method for calculating phase noise of reference microwave oscillators based on microwave MMIC amplifiers is considered. The calculations are based on the experimental dependence of amplifier phase noise on input power. Examples of calculation of microwave reference oscillators with an oscillatory system based on a dielectric resonator with unloaded Q factor of 20,000 are given. It is shown that using MMIC HMC-C072 as a part of such an oscillator, it is possible to achieve a phase noise level -136.8 dBc/Hz at 10 kHz offset for an operating frequency of 9.74 GHz.

articleTitle: Investigation of Scattering Intensity Dependencies on the Optical System Parameters in Cross-Correlation Spectrometer
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The cross-correlation method is an optical method used for studying particle sizes in liquid dispersed samples. In this work, we describe our estimations of the intensity of laser radiation scattering in a cross-correlation spectrometer depending on a number of parameters of the optical system, such as the focal length of the lens system, beam divergence, and the angle between incident beams. With help of presented calculations, one can increase the power of detected scattered signal and signal-to-noise ratio in cross-correlation spectrometers scheme.

articleTitle: Influence of Penetrating Radiation on Current- Voltage Characteristics of Complementary JFETs
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The change in the current-voltage characteristics (CVC) of silicon n-JFETs and p-JFETs when exposed to gamma rays <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">60</sup>Co and electrons with the energy of 6 MeV is considered. The obtained approximations of the dependences of the pinch-off voltage and drain current on the fluence of fast electrons are presented.

articleTitle: Means to Enhance the Bandwidth Gain from Applying Multicomponent Signals in DVB-S2
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: This paper considers the improvement of DVB-S2 system by using bandwidth-efficient multicomponent signals (MCS) with optimal shaping pulses. Finite optimal pulses are obtained by solving the optimization problem of minimizing partial correlation of pulses taking into account spectral mask. Optimal pulses with different ISI levels are considered to choose the best pulses for various signal-to-noise conditions. It is showed that the pulse with high ISI level performs better as signal-to-noise ratio increases. Moreover, increasing the number of iterations in LDPC decoding leads to more bandwidth efficiency gain for the system with optimal pulses. A practical realization based on USRP device of the DVB-S2 system with optimal pulses is supposed to confirm system performance in radio frequency channel.

articleTitle: Study of the Electrophysical Properties of Thin Films of Mixed Zinc and Tin Oxides
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: In this work, we studied the electrical properties of films of mixed zinc and tin oxides obtained by low-temperature pyrolysis. The temperature dependences of the resistance of ZnO-SnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> films, measured in the range from room temperature to 300 °C, showed the difference between the heating and cooling curves, which is explained by two competing processes - thermal generation of electrons and adsorption of oxygen particles on the surface of the oxide film. Using the slope of the linear section on the Arrhenius plot, we calculated the activation energy of conductivity, which amounted to 1.1 eV. Based on the results of energy dispersive analysis, it was concluded that the material of the obtained films is zinc oxide with the addition of tin oxide.

articleTitle: Semiconductor Sensor with Embedded Gate-control Potential Barriers
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: In this paper, we study the processes related to a semiconductor sensor detection of electromagnetic wave irradiation. The distribution of the electric potential and the motion of the charge carriers in the semiconductor sensor with embedded gate-control potential barriers are under investigation using the computer simulation software Comsol Multiphysics. For the first time, the dependence on the accumulated dynamic charge concentration of the potential barriers height as a value used in analytical models was obtained. The appropriate mechanism of potential barriers and charge carrier dynamics and some possible applications were revealed and estimated.

articleTitle: Multilayer Microstrip Bandpass Filter Design Using Galvanic Coupling
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: In this paper miniaturization of a microstrip bandpass filter using multilayer structure based on galvanic coupling between parts of half-wavelength resonator is discussed. Sample structure is realized for the frequency characteristics of a GPS receiver as an example, with a lower bandwidth limit in the L5 frequency band and an upper limit in the L2 frequency band, with a central frequency of 1.209 GHz. Proposed method can reduce the size by at least two times for MPL and more for multilayer technology.

articleTitle: Scaling QAM Technique for LED-based Visible Light Communication System with Signal-related Noise
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: We propose a scaling QAM technique considering the signal-related noise in a practical VLC system. Experiments are performed and the results indicate that the proposed scaling QAM can improve the performance of VLC system significantly.

articleTitle: Measurements and Stabilization of the Radio Signals Time Delay When Their Transmitting Over Long Wideband Analog Fiber Optics Links
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The results of measurements of the time delay in analog wideband fiber-optic links for microwave signal transmission are presented. Fiber-optic links operates in frequency range 0.1...18 GHz. The delay is determined by the results of measurements of the fiber-optic link phase-frequency response performed by using a vector network analyzer with a large number of points in the measuring trace. The length of the fiber-optic link in the experiments extends up to 1000 meters. The results of experiments on stabilizing the microwave signal delay at the fiber-optic link output using a fiber stretcher with piezoelectric control inserted in the link are also considered.

articleTitle: Fast, Efficient, and Radiation Hard ZnO:In Ceramic Scintillator
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Scintillating ceramics based on zinc oxide were prepared by the hot uniaxial pressing technique. Scintillating properties of ZnO:In ceramic are discussed and compared with the ZnO:Ga ceramic and a commercial organic scintillator BC-400 under X-ray and heavy ion irradiation. Indium admixture allows obtaining the desired effect of quenching of the slow luminescence and enhancement of fast one through the creation of shallow donors. In<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> doping is more effective than Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>: the maximum of fast luminescence intensity is 1.7 times higher in ZnO:In ceramics. The effect of annealing on the scintillation properties of ceramics was also studied.

articleTitle: Distortion Analysis of Interferometric Signal with Auxiliary Emission Modulation in Semiconductor Laser
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The results of distortion analysis of interferometric signal of a semiconductor laser with the current modulation are presented. The mathematical model of the interferometric signal was refined based on experimental data. Measurements were performed for harmonic and triangular auxiliary modulation, and the effect of laser thermal stabilization on the modulation of the interferometric signal was studied.

articleTitle: Algorithms of Processing and Analysis of Telemetric Information of Small Satellite of the "AIST" Series for the Purpose of Prompt Detection of Failures of on-Board Equipment
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The article considers some aspects of processing and analysis of telemetric information, received from the "AIST" small satellite constellation. The telemetric information is processed in order to identify and filter data entries that indicate equipment failures, using an algorithm, proposed by Medlin J.E. On the next step, the processed telemetric information has been analyzed. The analysis of the processed telemetric information resulted in the identification of the causes of failures, the most dangerous factors of the outer space and vulnerabilities of "AIST" small satellites.

articleTitle: Multiple Access for UWB Wireless Sensor Network System
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Ultra-wideband signals has been adopted in wireless sensor networks research due to its high performance in conditions of active influence of various noises and interferences, the presence of reflections and high data rates. In this paper, we consider one of the most important problems of telecommunication, i.e. the problem of multiple access. In our modeling, we address a scheme consisting of energy detector approach on the receiving side and on-of-keying modulation to decrease the system complexity and, hence, cost of an ultimate device. We compare different extending sequences for direct sequences multiple access method using Bit-Error-Rate (BER) estimation to reveal the best one for transmitting by only one user. The sequences considered are as follows: OOC, Walsh codes, M-sequences and Gold codes. Also, we produce assessment of characteristics of number of users equaled 5 to choose appropriate scheme of multiple access for simultaneous data transmission of many packets at the same time by one device. The obtained results explain the best choice for Aloha access control protocol and systems that utilize code division of channels of one device.

articleTitle: Peculiarities in the Formation of Multilayer Systems on the Basis of Porous Silicon
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Using scanning electron microscopy and infrared spectroscopy, some peculiarities in the formation of multilayer porous silicon were investigated. The effect of the changes in the current density during electrochemical etching of silicon on the composition of chemical bonds for the obtained porous structure was found.

articleTitle: The de Haas-van Alphen Effect in a Silicon Nanosandwich at the Room Temperature. Numerical Simulation of the Oscillations with Integer Filling Factors
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: We present a study of the high-temperature de Haas - van Alphen effect in a silicon nanostructure with integer filling factors up to ν = 11, inclusively. It is shown that the observed oscillations can be described by the model of the Gaussian broadening of the Landau levels of the twodimensional density of states and an energy-independent basis. The estimation of the magnitude of the carriers effective mass appears to be 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup> free electron mass.

articleTitle: AM Signal Finding in the Environment Full of Micro Doppler Shifts Using Bispectral Analysis
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The signal analysis using the power spectrum and autocorrelation function is insufficient as it does not provide complete information about signals because of the loss of the phase information in the power spectrum and autocorrelation function. In this case it is very important to use higher order statistics (HOS). We use HOS to distinguish between useful information and noise, with the procedure looking like carrier suppressed amplitude modulation. Matching of these two signals is described in the paper.

articleTitle: Lithium Niobate Films for Piezoelectric Nanogenerators Based on Hybrid Carbon Nanostructures
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: This work shows the experimental results of the effect of Ar + O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> background gas pressure under pulsed laser deposition on the formation of LiNbO3 films and their morphological properties. It was found that when the pressure of the Ar + O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> mixture increased from 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup> Torr to 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup> Torr, the grain diameter of the films decreased from (196±7) nm to (137±5) nm, and the obtained films at the pressure of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup> consisted of separate clusters with diameter (59±4) nm. Based on the obtained results, an architecture of piezoelectric nanogenerator was developed and its parameters were investigated.

articleTitle: One-dimensional Nanostructures of Conducting Polypyrrole: Preparation and Properties
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: In order to expand the possibilities of application of conducting polypyrrole, an optimized method for the synthesis of one-dimensional polymer nanostructures has been developed. By a simple one-step synthesis, polypyrrole is obtained in the form of uniform one-dimensional nanoparticles with diameter 90 nm and aspect ratio more than 50. It is shown that the main properties of one-dimensional polypyrrole (conductivity, specific surface area, absorption in near-infrared and stability) are superior to common bulk polymer with spherical structure of nanoparticles.

articleTitle: Approaching the Shannon Limit by Means of Optimal FTN Signals with Increased Size of PAM Signal Constellation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Application of Faster than Nyquist (FTN) signals allows achieving high spectral and energy characteristics of the communication system. Further approaching the Shannon limit that determines the channel throughput is related to increasing the size of the signal constellation. However, an increase in the size of the signal constellation results in sharp growth of energy losses for FTN signals. To reduce these energy losses optimal FTN pulses obtained as a result of solving the optimization problem with the constraint on signal constellation size M may be used. In this work, optimal pulse shapes for pulse-amplitude modulation (PAM) with M=4, 16, 64, 256 were found. It was shown that applying optimal FTN signals with PAM allows reducing energy losses by 4 dB regarding the FTN signals based on root-raised-cosine pulses for coherent symbol-by-symbol detection algorithm. In terms of approaching the Shannon limit, the closest results are provided by determining the bandwidth containing 99% of signal energy.

articleTitle: Localization of Ionizing Radiation Using Nanoporous Alumina Matrices
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The paper deals with ion beam transportation to the object of investigation. The passing and scattering of accelerated helium ions under irradiation of dielectric channels based on porous alumina were studied. The MSU accelerator complex HVEE AN-2500 was used as a source of the He<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> beam with an energy of 1.7 MeV. Scattering of ions was studied by means of RBS technique. Helium transition through nanoporous alumina was observed at various angles between the normal to the sample and the beam propagation direction. It is shown that porous anodic aluminum oxides have the structure of an ideal dielectric matrix of nanocapillaries. Due to the small angular scattering it allows transportation of the accelerated charged particle beams through the dielectric capillaries, and, as a result, the localization of high energy ionic effects.

articleTitle: Optimization of Spectral Characteristics of the Controlled Color-Dynamic Surgical Light Source for Visualization of Organs and Tissues of Laboratory Animals
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Modern LED light sources have many advantages for operational lighting. They make it possible to choose the optimal type of lighting for the surgeon during operations on certain organs and systems. The study was aimed at experimental selection of lighting parameters for various organs in vivo in normal and pathological conditions using a controlled color-dynamic LED lamp. The results showed that specific spectral parameters of lighting are necessary for certain types of organs and tissues; color and light balance adjusting improves the contrast visualization of individual tissues relative to each other. This work is the initial stage of creation of a special atlas of light source parameters for visualization of organs and tissues during surgical interventions with the use of controlled color-dynamic surgical light source.

articleTitle: Effective Mode Volume Evolution in the He-Ne Laser
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: It has been introduced the concept of the effective mode volume and its modification taking into account the population inversion distribution of the active medium in this paper. The He-Ne laser output power values were calculated using the effective mode volume that is consistent with the experimental data and the power values were estimated by the other methods.

articleTitle: The Multi-Criteria Optimization in the LTspice Simulation Software of a JFet class AB Buffer Amplifier for Operation at Low Temperatures
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: A high-speed buffer amplifier (BA) for analog microcircuits on complementary junction field-effect transistors is proposed. The scheme differs from the known circuit solutions by a small number of elements and can operate within the range of cryogenic temperatures. In the LTSpice simulation software, the optimal control parameters were selected using the DEAP (Distributed Evolutionary Algorithm in Python) library of distributed evolutionary calculations and the NSGA-II multi-criteria optimization algorithm. Minimization of offset voltage, static current consumption and dead band width on the amplitude characteristic at low temperatures were chosen as the priority parameters of the control unit.

articleTitle: Method for Platinum Group Metals Extraction from SiC Based Catalyst Carrier
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The team of authors described the solution to the problem of developing a fundamentally new technology for the industrial processing of spent diesel automotive catalysts containing platinum group metals (PGM) and SiC carrier, which has such advantage as carrying out a full processing cycle in one hardware module. The processing of SiC catalyst is extremely difficult by pyrometallurgical methods, but proposed technology is based on the electrochlorination method. The scientific novelty of the proposed method lies in the superposition of two independent electrolysis processes in direct and alternating, with varying frequency, currents under conditions of forced, continuous, and complete recondensation of the electrolyte. The study of the diesel catalysts processing by the electrochlorination method have been carried out.

articleTitle: Strontium Bismuthate Sr3Bi2O6: Thermostimulated Change of Optical Properties and its Analysis from the Point of View of Urbach Rule
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Data on the temperature dependence of the optical properties of Sr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Bi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> strontium bismuthate are given. Several linear sections were found on the diffuse reflection spectra on a logarithmic scale. It was shown that additional linear regions can be associated with electrons localized at deep biographical defects of the crystal lattice. For all detected linear sections, the main parameters of electron-phonon interactions are determined.

articleTitle: Taking into Account Noise and Background Information During Transmitting of Decisions on Signal Detection-Estimation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The article considers problems of detecting and estimating the coordinates of small-sized space objects with onboard passive television systems, observed against a starry background, from a standpoint of the principle of dominant information. The asymmetry of detection threshold that ensures sufficient equality of losses of dominant and noise information, is substantiated. This is achieved by equalizing probability of missing the signal of object and probability of false alarm, multiplied by the number of degrees of freedom of the signal.

articleTitle: Opportunities of Scanning Spreading Resistance Microscopy for Photosensitive Nanostructured Materials Characterization
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The possibilities and features of the application of scanning spreading resistance microscopy (SSRM) methods and original methods developed at SPbETU "LETI" (Department of Micro- and Nanoelectronics, UNL "Nanomaterials") for studying the electrical and physical properties and structure of photosensitive polycrystalline layers of lead chalcogenides, including the possibility of a qualitative analysis of the composition of oxide coatings of such layers are considered.

articleTitle: Application of Multi-element Photo Detector in Optical Disdrometers
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The design of multi-element silicon photodetector for optical disdrometer, which allows reducing the measurement error of intensity, size and speed of meteorological precipitation has been developed. The parameters of the pulses of the photocurrent arising at the intersection of the shadows of the moving particles of the photosensitive elements of the photodetector are analyzed. Additional (in comparison with the standard design) photosensitive elements of the rectangular receiver, located perpendicular to the standard operating elements of the photodetector, allows us to take into account the influence of edge effects when performing digital signal processing. It is shown that the boundary effects arising at the intersection of the shadow of the particle of the photosensitive element edge can lead to an error in the measurement of the size and intensity of meteorological precipitation up to 30% at the raindrops diameters of 2... 5 mm. Developed software, taking into account the constructive and functional characteristics of the sensor when processing the signals, allows us to reduce the error probability by 1-2 orders of magnitude to a value of 1.5...2%. The algorithm of signal processing is described. The results of the tests of the developed photodetector as a part of an optical disdrometer are presented.

articleTitle: Clarification of the Phase Diagram of PbHfO3 in Pressure-temperature Space
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: We report the high-temperature and high-pressure single-crystal x-ray diffraction study of PbHfO3. The increase of pressure enables an additional intermediate phase, located between the cubic and incommensurate phases, and characterized by superstructure reflections indicating the presence of anti-phase oxygen octahedral tilts. The temperature-dependent diffuse peak at an incommensurate position is much better pronounced at higher pressures (~ 2 GPa) than at lower pressures (~ 1.1 GPa), which we interpret as enhancing of the incommensurate soft mode on pressure increase. Several peculiarities in the behavior of superstructural reflections at M- and X- points are reported and discussed.

articleTitle: Perspectives for Appliance and Accuracy Improvement of Coordinate Measurements with Laser Technique
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: This paper describes some practical problems of coordinates measuring concerning both linear and angular measurements. The trade-off between the measuring accuracy and maximum range was pointed out as a central issue in Geometrical Dimensioning and Tolerancing (GD&T) inspection. The opportunity for online measurements for manufacturing industries has also been described. An implementation of the advanced commercial measuring system in relation to GD&T has been demonstrated in this work.

articleTitle: Mode Division Multiplexing as a Technique Counteracting Intrusion to Multimode Fiber Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The presented material shows that a fruitful way to counteract illegal data reading from the system trunk fiber could be application of mode division multiplexing technique, particularly under special manner of data transmission via the few- or multimode trunk fiber. The principle of namely data distributive technique is described. The content of the technique include division of the data sequence to time periods each containing several data blocks and simultaneous transmission of these blocks over different modes of the trunk fiber. If eavesdropping occurs, the illegally registered signal is a mix of different data blocks. Transmission of random signals via the extra fiber mode could provide additional impeding of decoding the illegally read data. At the end of the line, reversal processing of the received data restores the original data sequence. Advantageous feature of the technique is full compatibility with all developed methods of data security. Cooperative application of these techniques could enhance the protection of transmitted data.

articleTitle: Spectral Analysis of Surfaces of Newly Formed Regenerative Tissues After Chondroplasty with Plated-Rich Plasma
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The results of research of articular surfaces of distal femoral epiphyses in rabbits that had different types of plasty of articular cartilage defects using Raman spectroscopy method is presented. The component analysis of sample surfaces has been made using spectra deconvolution by spectral contour selection. The efficiency of the method of substitution of hyaline cartilage full-layer defects by the combination of platelet-rich plasma and demineralized bone-plastic material is shown. It has been established that Raman spectroscopy can be used for estimation of surfaces of new-formed tissues after chondroplasty.

articleTitle: Low-loss Polymer Optical Components and Cladding Interferometric Devices Inscribed Using Femtosecond Laser Inscription
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: We present the development of low-loss polymer optical fiber components and interferometric devices in perfluorinated multimode fibers like CYTOP and silica fibers, respectively. This includes the inscription of usable fiber Bragg gratings, chirped gratings and Fabry-Perot cavities in multimode gradient index fiber using a femtosecond laser inscription. We present the successful demonstration of interferometric devices such as Mach-Zehnder filters and Fabry-Perot cavities inscribed in the cladding of a single mode silica optical fiber. The advantages of these particular progressive sensors are discussed.

articleTitle: Estimation of the Irradiated Graphite Surface Nanolayer Thickness Enriched by 14С Isotope
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: In the present paper we evaluate the thickness of the reactor graphite surface nanolayer enriched by <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14</sup>C isotope formed during reactor operation. This graphite surface <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14</sup>C enriched nanolayer is proposed to be removed using our new inert gas plasma decontamination technology. Surface decontamination of the nuclear power plant (NPP) constructions is provided by ion bombardment of the nano- and micro-sized radionuclides layer from the surface under treatment (cathode) and their diffusive transfer to collector plate (anode). There are many evidences that, e.g. <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14</sup>C is predominantly located on the surface of irradiated reactor graphite instead of the inside of the graphite bulk. It is due to <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14</sup>C main formation mechanism via effective neutron activation of the gaseous nitrogen, which is used as a coolant of the graphite piles. So, it is important to find N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> molecules concentration and subsurface depth penetration inside of graphite samples. In this way plasma sputtering technology can significantly reduce the irradiated reactor graphite activity at the decommissioning of uranium-graphite reactors. Additionally, this technology can be used to separate various atomic species sputtered from the graphite sample (together with their radioactive isotopes) by their sedimentation temperature and to form nanosized layer enriched with preferred radionuclides of controlled thickness. It provides to obtain new materials like a beta-active "nano-micro-sandwich" with adjusted output fast electrons energy spectrum. It can be used in the nuclear medicine field and for a new type of the betavoltaic batteries.

articleTitle: Reflective Deep Relief Structure with Variable Depth Produced by the Action of Modified Femtosecond Laser Radiation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: This article describes a method of manufacturing a deep relief structure of variable depth, based on the chemical etching of glass modified by femtosecond laser radiation. An effective model of deep relief structure of variable depth, suitable for use in optical filters, is proposed.

articleTitle: Composite Porous Silicon Materials for Emission Electrode Synthesis
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The theoretical background of the electron field emission process is provided, both contemporary and perspective emission models are considered. Porous silicon (PS) based nanostructured material functionalized with fullerenol is suggested for further electrode realization for both field and photon enhanced thermionic emission processes due to its unique properties. The synthesis technique of composite PS-C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">60</inf>OH/Ag+Cu prototype structure required for further emitter electrode realization is developed.

articleTitle: Thermoelectric Properties of Bismuth Telluride and Antimony Telluride Synthesized by Electrochemical Deposition Method
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The paper presents the study of thermoelectric properties of bismuth telluride and antimony telluride obtained by electrochemical deposition method. Measurements of electrical conductivity and the Seebeck coefficient were carried out on a NETZCH SBA 458 Nemesis® measuring setup. The coefficient value of bismuth telluride accounted for –47 µV/K, and the coefficient value of bismuth telluride made up 20 µV/K.
